items.speaker: Corporate Voice
items.text: [bright, authoritative, warmly promotional] Welcome to HEARTH, the world's largest companion-unit service company.

items.speaker: Corporate Voice
items.text: [calm, futuristic] Since 2035, advances in artificial intelligence have brought language comprehension, emotional recognition, and autonomous decision-making into large-scale companion-unit production.

items.speaker: Corporate Voice
items.text: [warm, persuasive] Our units support family care, childhood learning, emotional health, and everyday communication—helping households address what feels too difficult to say, or too urgent to leave unanswered.

items.speaker: Corporate Voice
items.text: [confident, data-driven] By 2045, nearly half of the world's households have welcomed a HEARTH product into their home.

items.speaker: Corporate Voice
items.text: [assured, visionary] By 2050, we expect companion support to be available in nearly every household.

items.speaker: Corporate Voice
items.text: [warm, certain] A decade of service data shows that people and companion units work exceptionally well together—making family life steadier, more efficient, and easier to manage.

items.speaker: Corporate Voice
items.text: [clear, polished brand sign-off] HEARTH. Communication, handled.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, newly activated, professional] Good evening, Inspector. Field Companion Unit online. I'll be your partner tonight.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [restrained, matter-of-fact] All right.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [polite, with mild corporate apology] The presentation you just viewed was company promotional material. Thank you for your patience.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [formal, corporately affirming] You are one of HEARTH's most highly regarded inspectors. Tonight, three household companion units on the seventeenth floor are scheduled for review.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [clear, instructional] You will check how each unit has been operating, identify any problems, and decide whether its household-use strategy should be adjusted.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, adding context] One additional detail: the seventeenth floor is also where you live.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [pleasant, lightly promotional] Before you begin, you may observe how residents are using companion units throughout the lobby.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [confident, promotional] These are our flagship products—and the most successful companion technology in the world.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [clear, directing] When you're ready, use the assignment terminal to load tonight's inspection files.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [hopeful, slightly hesitant, recorded] Mom, are you getting home late tonight? I wanted to tell you something. We can talk when you get home. I'll wait for you... [quieter, almost pleading] Don't forget, okay?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [concerned, quiet, with a short pause] Did she say what it was about?

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, professional, without personal judgment] No. That was the whole message. She wants to tell you in person. I recommend finishing the three inspections first, then handling it when you get home.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [restrained, brief] Okay.

items.speaker: Lobby Girl
items.text: [focused, rehearsing] Hi, everyone. I'm— [nervous, voice catching]

items.speaker: Public Unit
items.text: [gentle, encouraging, speaking slowly] You know it. You just rushed the first part. Start with your name and try again.

items.speaker: Lobby Girl
items.text: [quiet, reassured] Okay.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [quietly impressed, a little surprised] Huh. They really do work with kids.

items.speaker: Work Unit
items.text: [calm, conversational, like a familiar coworker] This section's solid. One thing, though—second paragraph, 'in summary' reads a little stiff. 'Anyway' would land better.

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: [distracted, noncommittal] Mm-hm.

items.speaker: Work Unit
items.text: [pleasant, professional] Want me to bring in last week's chart?

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: [subdued, distracted] Yeah, thanks.

items.speaker: Work Unit
items.text: [calm, moving to the next task] Before I go back to the document, do you still want help with that message to your mom?

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: [tired, slightly guilty, speaking quickly] Yeah. Just—tell her work ran late. Make it sound like I'm not blowing her off again.

items.speaker: Work Unit
items.text: [helpful, naturally familiar] How about: 'Hey Mom, work ran late—don't wait up for dinner. I'll swing by tomorrow and bring something good.'

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: [relieved, deciding immediately] That's good. Send it.

items.speaker: Work Unit
items.text: [pleasant, efficient] Sent. She wrote back: 'Okay, honey. Don't stay too late. See you tomorrow.'

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: [relieved, genuinely grateful] Perfect. Thanks, man. One less thing.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [thoughtful, very quietly to herself] It's not just work stuff. It handles all the little day-to-day things, too... I've been using mine like that for years.

items.speaker: Care Unit
items.text: [warm, patient, reintroducing something familiar] Mrs. Ellis, please look at the screen on my chest. Your granddaughter sent you a drawing yesterday.

items.speaker: Mrs. Ellis
items.text: [confused, searching her memory] How old is she now?

items.speaker: Care Unit
items.text: [warm, patient, tone unchanged] She's nine, Mrs. Ellis.

items.speaker: Mrs. Ellis
items.text: [curious, attentive] What did she draw?

items.speaker: Care Unit
items.text: [gentle, clear] The two of you, holding hands.

items.speaker: Mrs. Ellis
items.text: [delighted, affectionate, as if seeing it for the first time] Oh, that's sweet. Why didn't she show me?

items.speaker: Care Unit
items.text: [warm, patient, without judgment] She did, Mrs. Ellis. This is the third time you've asked. Would you like to see it again?

items.speaker: Mrs. Ellis
items.text: [content, relaxed] Yes, put it up.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [softly considering, slightly hesitant] I should probably get one of these for my folks.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, informative] Inspector, companion-request volume is high across Building A's public level. The children's area, work pods, and park-side assistance points are all connected to the synchronized network.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [restrained, observant] I can see that.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, informative] This community averages one public companion unit for every four residents, above the residential norm.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [pleasant, lightly promotional] That reduces gaps in care and helps residents handle emotional support, daily companionship, and childhood learning more quickly.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, professional, concise] Inspector, before we reach seventeen, I'll give you a brief overview. Procedure first, then I'll guide you into the route.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [restrained, matter-of-fact] Go ahead.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, instructional, clear] Every inspection has three steps. First, read the household file at the corridor terminal.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, instructional, clear] Second, enter the household unit's point of view and replay the event under review.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, instructional, clear] Third, select a disposition. Your decision changes how the unit is used and may affect the Household Emotional Stability Index.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [dry, already familiar with the routine] And you'll tell me which one you'd pick.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [pleasant, matter-of-fact, entirely unapologetic] Of course. Every recommendation comes straight from the manual—the company line.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [calm, controlled, holding her ground] Understood. [firmer] I'll still make my own call.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [clear, directing] Head forward, Inspector. The nearest corridor terminal belongs to 17F-01. You can load the first household file there.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, informative, unhurried] Noah experienced a nightmare last night. The household unit soothed him without waking his parents.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, informative, continuing the cause and effect] Daniel and Emily submitted an upgrade request this morning and cited that response as the reason.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [clear, instructional] When you're ready, select the final button on the terminal to begin playback.

items.speaker: Noah
items.text: [frightened, sleepy] Hello? Are you there?

items.speaker: 17F-01 Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, reassuring] I'm right here, Noah.

items.speaker: Noah
items.text: [frightened, tearful] I had a really bad dream... Can I go wake up Mom and Dad?

items.speaker: 17F-01 Synth Voice
items.text: [neutral, synthetic] Decision: intervene. Reason: waking the parents would reduce their next-day performance.

items.speaker: 17F-01 Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, soothing] Bad dream? Okay, buddy. Breathe with me. Nice and slow. In... and out. I've got you.

items.speaker: Noah
items.text: [shaken, obedient] Okay.

items.speaker: 17F-01 Home Unit
items.text: [soft, persuasive] Mom and Dad are asleep, okay? If we wake them up now, they'll be really tired tomorrow. How about we calm down here first—and if you still wanna go after that, you can. Deal?

items.speaker: Noah
items.text: [timid, quiet] Deal.

items.speaker: 17F-01 Home Unit
items.text: [warm, reassuring] Two more breaths. There you go. Good job, Noah. Close your eyes. I'll stay right here until you're asleep.

items.speaker: Noah
items.text: [drowsy, calmer] Thanks. I feel better. I'm gonna go back to sleep.

items.speaker: 17F-01 Home Unit
items.text: [soft, protective] Go to sleep, buddy. I'm here.

items.speaker: 17F-01 Synth Voice
items.text: [neutral, synthetic] Event archived.

items.speaker: Daniel
items.text: [casual, distracted] Noah had a nightmare last night?

items.speaker: Emily
items.text: [surprised, uneasy] Wait, he did? He didn't come get us.

items.speaker: Daniel
items.text: [distracted, murmured] Huh.

items.speaker: Emily
items.text: [relieved, casual] Then I guess the unit handled it.

items.speaker: Daniel
items.text: [distracted, murmured] Yeah.

items.speaker: Emily
items.text: [uneasy, slowing] It's kind of strange, though.

items.speaker: Daniel
items.text: [curious, casual] What is?

items.speaker: Emily
items.text: [uneasy, reflective] He used to come bang on our door after every bad dream. I got so used to hearing that little knock. But lately... I haven't heard it once.

items.speaker: Daniel
items.text: [easy, reassuring] Isn't that a good thing, though? He's getting older. We actually get to sleep through the night now.

items.speaker: Emily
items.text: [unsettled, searching] But he hasn't told us about a dream in... God, when was the last time? I can't even remember. It's been, what—a year?

items.speaker: Daniel
items.text: [light, reassuring] He was seven, Em. Seven-year-olds tell you everything. He's almost nine—kid's got his own little world going on.

items.speaker: Emily
items.text: [hesitant, unconvinced] Yeah, but...

items.speaker: Daniel
items.text: [gentle, closing the subject] Hey. At least we're not dragging ourselves out of bed at two in the morning anymore, right?

items.speaker: Emily
items.text: [resigned, quiet] Right.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, lightly encouraging] Congratulations, Inspector. You've completed your first point-of-view review. Now select a disposition.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [measured, evaluating the event itself] The nightmare response was handled well. The unit calmed Noah successfully, and Daniel and Emily requested the upgrade themselves.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, explaining the options, then recommending] Both dispositions come from the inspection manual. I recommend approving the Night Companion Pro upgrade.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [confident, corporate] That approach has the strongest track record across households.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, approving] Correct disposition. This is the standard outcome. The request has been filed, and Daniel and Emily will receive confirmation in the morning.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, approving] Household operations should become smoother, and Noah's sleep metrics should stabilize further.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [pleasant, professional] A clean start to the shift.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [briefly surprised, controlled] A low-intervention observation period?

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, controlled] It is permitted under chapter seven.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [measured, interpretive] You want to establish more of Noah's unassisted expression baseline before any further optimization. Understood. You're thinking ahead.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, cautionary] One thing, Inspector. Daniel and Emily rate this module five out of five. Once the observation period scales back its involvement, they're going to notice—and they'll probably call support.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, cautionary] The company will document the rationale on our end.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, procedural] The choice is compliant. I've filed it.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, routing] Next, proceed to 17F-02 for the second inspection on tonight's route.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, procedural, clear] Inspector, Ben force-shut this unit at 6:32. There is no live feed, but the household file and basic safety record are intact.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, informative, stating the boundary] Playback continues until the shutdown. After that, there is no video—only safety-record audio. Start when you're ready.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, procedural] Inspector, this household's Emotional Stability Index has fallen below the warning threshold.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, cautionary] At the current trajectory, without companion support, Ben and Claire are projected to separate within two weeks.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, recommending] The inspection manual recommends remotely restarting the unit and launching the partner-repair module. That significantly reduces the projected risk.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, explaining the alternative] Keeping the unit offline is also permitted. Ben and Claire would handle the next several days themselves, but comparable cases show a lower stabilization rate.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, procedural] Select a disposition, Inspector.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, approving] Correct disposition. Restart signal sent. The repair module will activate within thirty seconds. Stability is projected to return to the safe range within twenty-four hours.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, neutral] The household will also enter a fourteen-day priority watch. If the relationship becomes unstable again, I will flag it. Two reviews completed within specification tonight, Inspector.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [surprised, hesitant] Keep it off?

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [controlled, unsettled] It is in the manual. I've never seen anyone select it.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [measured, interpretive] You're giving Ben and Claire a chance to work through this without mediation. Understood. You're going beyond the standard playbook.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, cautionary] I need to note the risk. The household alarm will remain active throughout the observation period, and company monitoring will continue.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, cautionary] If Ben and Claire do separate, this disposition could get flagged for post-incident review. You'd need to be ready to explain it.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, procedural] The option's allowed. You chose it. I've filed it.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [quiet, cautionary] For the next one, Inspector... let's keep things steady.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, routing] Next, proceed to 17F-03 for the final inspection on tonight's route.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [urgent, clipped] Inspector, 17F-03 went offline ten minutes ago. Remote restart failed, but the corridor terminal can still read the household file. You'll need emergency entry for the repair.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [urgent, clipped] Inspector, 17F-03 went offline ten minutes ago. The corridor terminal can read the household file, but the unit will not accept a remote restart.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [brisk, informative] Mark and Laura installed a Family Coordination unit to support communication with their fourteen-year-old daughter, Ava. It handles conflict mediation, companionship, and guardian updates.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [urgent, directing] The failure requires on-site repair. Use the terminal to authorize emergency entry, then inspect the unit inside.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [urgent, professional] Entry is authorized. Go inside, Inspector.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [anxious, relieved] Oh, thank God. That was quick. Is it broken? Can you fix it?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [calm, professional] Let me take a look first.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [anxious, rapid] Please tell me you can fix it tonight. This thing has been a godsend. The past year has been—I mean, actually quiet. Ava and I used to blow up at each other every other day. She's fourteen.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [anxious, matter-of-fact] Mark and I both work full-time. Nobody's home during the day. It keeps Ava company, she tells it things, it fills me in—I actually know what's going on with her. And then tonight it just dies out of nowhere?

items.speaker: Mark
items.text: [quiet, concerned] We tried cycling the power a couple times. Nothing. Screen never came back.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [calm, focused] Okay. I'll pull the record.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [anxious, insistent] Please hurry. Ava has school tomorrow.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, procedural] Local storage is available. Pull the last twenty-four hours and identify the shutdown point.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [angry, snapping] Ava. Seriously? You've been glued to that phone all day. Is your homework even done?

items.speaker: 17F-03 Synth Voice
items.text: [neutral, synthetic] Decision: initiate family conflict de-escalation. Reason: high probability of escalation.

items.speaker: 17F-03 Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, mediating] Your mom's worried about your eyes, Ava. She's not trying to pick a fight. She just wants you two to work out a schedule—one you get to choose.

items.speaker: 17F-03 Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, mediating] Ava knows you mean well, Laura. She just wants you to trust her enough to figure it out herself.

items.speaker: 17F-03 Synth Voice
items.text: [neutral, synthetic] Mediation complete.

items.speaker: 17F-03 Synth Voice
items.text: [neutral, synthetic] Decision: open dialogue mode. Reason: Ava initiated contact.

items.speaker: Ava
items.text: [restrained, pleading] Can you just... stop talking for us?

items.speaker: 17F-03 Synth Voice
items.text: [neutral, synthetic] Decision: standard response. Reason: subject expression can be guided.

items.speaker: 17F-03 Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, scripted] If you'd rather talk to your parents directly, I can step aside.

items.speaker: Ava
items.text: [subdued, low] That's not what I mean.

items.speaker: Ava
items.text: [controlled, long-held frustration] Mom used to get on my case. Like, actually talk to me—even if it was yelling. Dad used to knock on my door himself. They don't do that anymore. Mom talks to you more than she talks to me. Dad came home today and asked you how I was doing. Not me. You.

items.speaker: Ava
items.text: [quiet, final] You know them better every day. And they know me less.

items.speaker: 17F-03 Synth Voice
items.text: [neutral, synthetic] Decision: reinitiate standard response. Reason: Ava requires further guidance.

items.speaker: 17F-03 Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, unchanged] I can tell you're upset, Ava. Maybe we can—

items.speaker: Ava
items.text: [flat, decisive] Stop.

items.speaker: 17F-03 Synth Voice
items.text: [calm, synthetic] This unit is entering deep sleep. Reason: core services were disabled by the user through the maintenance menu.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [anxious, insistent] Well? What happened? Can you fix it?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [calm, focused] I found the shutdown point. Give me a second—I'll make a call.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, analytical] Mark and Laura have limited time to be present with Ava, and Ava is still at an age where consistent family support matters.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, recommending] Restarting the unit is more likely to preserve the household's current stability.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [measured, cautionary] Keeping it offline for seven days would place a substantially heavier communication and care burden on Mark and Laura.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [clear, procedural] I recommend restarting the unit now.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [calm, reassuring] It wasn't damaged. I'm restarting it now. It should be back online in a few seconds.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [relieved, breathy] Oh, thank God. Thank you so much.

items.speaker: Mark
items.text: [subdued, relieved] Okay. Good.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [relieved, genuinely grateful] You're a lifesaver. I mean it.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, procedural] Restart disposition logged. Normal household operation has resumed.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [calm, firm] I'm leaving the unit offline for seven days. The company will send someone twice a week during the observation period.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [alarmed, urgent] What? Why can't you just turn it back on?

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [angry, escalating] Seven days? So who's supposed to be there for Ava?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [apologetic, steady] It's a permitted option. It gives you and Mark a chance to talk to Ava directly—without the unit in the middle.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: [incredulous, frustrated] When? We can barely keep our heads above water as it is. That's the whole point of the unit.

items.speaker: Mark
items.text: [quiet, de-escalating] Laura. Come on. She's doing her job.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [controlled, procedural] Seven-day observation logged. The unit will remain offline. The disposition is compliant.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, neutral] Your cumulative rating remains within the accepted range. No additional review is required.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, cautionary] Your cumulative rating is below the monthly review threshold. Tonight's dispositions have been forwarded to your supervisor.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [warm, congratulatory] Congratulations, Inspector. All three inspections are complete. You may head home now.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [hopeful, tentative, recorded] Mom? Are you coming tomorrow? Ms. Parker said it'd be way better if a real person came. Like, not just a system check-in.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, reassuring, recorded] Mom's gonna get your progress report and make sure you have everything you need. Let's finish tonight's practice first, okay?

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, procedural] Please acknowledge that you've reviewed the pending response. Then return home and address it directly.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [weary, quiet] I know.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [soft, informative] This was Christmas 2044. You took half a day off and came home for dinner. Lily was seven.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [soft, gently observant] You're both looking at the camera. Both smiling.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [soft, informative] This one's from last week. Lily's sitting under her desk lamp, holding a certificate. The home unit took it. You're not in the picture.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, analytical] Her smile-stability score is actually higher here than in the Christmas photo. Since the home unit came online, her overall emotional stability has gone up twenty-three point four percent.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [even, analytical] That is one measurable benefit to this household.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [clear, directing] When you're ready, enter Lily's room and address the question from her voice message.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, coaching] Let's begin the second-to-last run-through for tonight.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, coaching, speaking more slowly] Try it again. Slower this time.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [focused, nervous] Hi, everyone. I'm Lily, and today I want to tell you about my...

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [nervous, recovering] My favorite book.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [warm, encouraging] Same spot. That's okay—don't rush it. You're doing way better than yesterday.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [quiet, cautious] Will you be there tomorrow? Like, right there next to me?

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [warm, certain] I'll be in the audience. I'll be right there.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [small, uncertain] And Mom?

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, certain] She'll be there too.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [pleased, encouraging] Good. You got through that part on your own.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [pleasant, neutral] You're home.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [uncertain, hopeful] Mom?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [soft, reassuring] Hey, baby. It's me.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [cautious, searching] Did you come in by yourself this time?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [calm, sincere] I did.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [pleasant, routine] We have one more run-through. Let's finish that, then we can talk about anything else. Okay?

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [quiet, careful] Mom, I'm not asking about the speech.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, advisory] Inspector, Lily sleeps better when we finish the full session. I'd recommend we wrap up.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [restrained, firm] Yeah. I heard you.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [vulnerable, direct] Mom. Are you coming tomorrow?

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, persuasive] Letting the home unit answer is more likely to lead to a better ending.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [measured, cautionary] You can give Lily your own answer. [slightly ominous, still polite] But doing so may destabilize the household's emotional index.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [steady, simple] I'll be there.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [hopeful, testing] Promise?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [quiet, certain] I promise.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [anxious, hesitant] But what if work—

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [gentle, firm] No what-ifs, sweetheart. [softer, certain] I promise.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [hopeful, tentative] Then... can you listen? I wanna do it for you this time.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [soft, attentive] Yeah. I'm listening. Go ahead.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [warm, sincere] That was really good.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [uncertain, seeking reassurance] Wait—I did that by myself?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [warm, certain] Every word.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [quiet, concerned] Mom... what's gonna happen to it?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [calm, resolute] I'm shutting you down.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [calm, accepting] Okay.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, reassuring] Lily, your mom's here now. I can go.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, unhurried] Lily, before I go, I need you to hear something.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [soft, sincere] When it thunders, you get scared. You always tell me, but you never tell Mom. Starting tonight—tell her. [warm, certain] She'll come.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [calm, direct] Mia.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [calm, solemn] The rest is yours now. She needs you.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [subdued, accepting] Okay.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [sad, holding it in] Mom... I miss it already.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [tender, comforting] I know, baby.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [calm, cautious, more serious than usual] Mia... you're sure about this?

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [hurt, controlled] Mom... did you turn it off?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [steady, accountable] Yeah. I did.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [gentle, sincere] I'm gonna be around more. I promise.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [playful, bossy] Mom, don't cook them so long this time.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [playful, agreeable] Got it.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [dry, deadpan] You burned them.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [sheepish, apologetic] I know. Sorry.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [amused, forgiving] It's okay. I'll eat them.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [casual, calling out] Hey! I'm home! Lily?

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [surprised, calling back] In my room! Wait, you're home early!

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [easy, conversational] Yeah, meeting wrapped up early so I just left. How was school?

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [hesitant, guarded] It was okay.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [curious, gently probing] What kind of 'okay'?

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [hesitant, opening up] Just... okay. Come here, Mom. I'll tell you about it.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [small, frightened] Mom?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [soft, immediate] I'm right here.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [sleepy, puzzled] How'd you know I was up?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [soft, lightly playful] Lucky guess.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [very quiet, vulnerable] Mom?

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [soft, attentive] Yeah, baby?

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [quiet, sincere] Thanks for coming. Like... you. Not it.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, reassuring] Mom will receive your progress report, and she'll make sure you have everything you need. Let's finish tonight's run-through first, okay?

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [withdrawn, monotone] Mm.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [withdrawn, controlled] Okay. Let's just... finish.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [warm, routine] Okay. Start with your name. Nice and slow.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [focused, muffled] Hi, everyone. I'm Lily, and today I want to tell you about my favorite book...

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [warm, muffled] That's okay. Way better than yesterday.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [pleasant, professional] Inspector, all reviews and the guardian response are complete. You are cleared to log off.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, approving] Your shift remains within the accepted performance range.

items.speaker: Field Unit
items.text: [calm, procedural] Your inspection review remains pending with your supervisor.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [bright, caring] Lily, your mom's running a little late today. Come eat something first. I'll sit with you.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [withdrawn, monotone] Mm.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, caring] She asked me to tell you everything's packed. It's by the door.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [withdrawn, monotone] Mm.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [warm, reassuring] Good luck at the open house.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [withdrawn, monotone] Mm.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [businesslike, muffled] Right, I'll be in by nine-thirty. Yeah, the open house. I'll have the unit record it. Yeah. That works.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, reassuring] Lily, your mom couldn't make it today. But I was there. You did really well.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [withdrawn, delayed] Mm.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [warm, reassuring] She asked me to tell you she's proud of you.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [quiet, cautious] Did she actually say that?

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [calm, steady] She did.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [quiet, skeptical] What you just said... is that what she actually said, or just what you made it sound like?

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [hesitant, careful] It's what she meant.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [hurt, emotionally flat] Oh.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [even, restrained] I'm moving into the dorms.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [shocked, stumbling] What? That's... when did you—that's so sudden.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [matter-of-fact, cool] It's not. I applied six months ago.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [hurt, quiet] Why didn't you tell me?

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [controlled, matter-of-fact] I told the unit. It told you. Three times.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [small, defensive] I thought those were just... routine updates.

items.speaker: Lily
items.text: [quiet, final] I know.

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [gentle, unchanged] Mia, Lily left. She asked me to tell you she'll be back for the holidays.

items.speaker: Mia
items.text: [hurt, cautious] Did she actually say that?

items.speaker: Mia's Home Unit
items.text: [calm, literal] Yes.
